chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Maymun, who said:
Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him, arrived performing tamattu‘ on the night of ‘Arafah. He performed tawaf, exited ihram, approached one of his servant women, then entered ihram for hajj and went out.

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: he exited the state of ihram
key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: he entered into the consecrated state for hajj
key_terms.فَطَافَ: he performed tawaf around the Ka‘bah
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: the night preceding or associated with the day of ‘Arafah

ai.seo_question: Can a person still perform tamattu‘ if they arrive on the night of ‘Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام arrived on the night of ‘Arafah in the state of tamattu‘, performed tawaf, exited ihram, and then re-entered ihram for hajj. It indicates the practical sequence of actions associated with tamattu‘ hajj and serves as evidence in jurisprudential discussions about the time at which one may still be considered to have performed tamattu‘.
